info.title: Kitsu API
info.description:
## Welcome to the Kitsu API specification ```Version: 1.1.0``` The Kitsu API allows to store and manage the data of your animation/VFX production. Through it you can link all the tools of your pipeline and make sure they are all synchronized. An easy to use Python client to access this API is available: [Python Kitsu Client documentation](https://gazu.cg-wire.com/) ## Authentication

Before you can use any of the endpoints outlined below, you will need to obtain a JWT token to authorize your requests.

You will find detailed information on how to retrieve authentication tokens in the [Zou documentation](https://zou.cg-wire.com/api/).

All API requests require authentication via JWT tokens passed in the Authorization header.

post.description: Log in a user and get authentication tokens. The email field accepts the email address or the desktop login of the user. Desktop tools that do not know the email address use the desktop login. If the user has two-factor authentication, give one second factor. The organisation has the chat tokens only for an administrator.

email.description: Email address or desktop login of the user

totp.description: TOTP code from the authenticator app

email_otp.description: One-time password that the user got by email

fido_authentication_response.description: Response of the FIDO device to the challenge

recovery_code.description: One recovery code of the user

200.description: The login is successful. If the instance enforces two-factor authentication and the user has not set it up, the body has two_factor_authentication_required and the tokens only give access to the authentication routes until the setup is done.

400.description: The login failed. The body tells the cause with the flags default_password, missing_OTP, wrong_OTP or too_many_failed_login_attemps. A wrong email and a wrong password give the same answer.

401.description: The user is inactive. The body has the flag unactive.

409.description: The authentication strategy is not correctly configured

500.description: The database is not available, or a server error occurred

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST "http://api.example.com/auth/login" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "email": "admin@example.com",
  "password": "mysecretpassword",
  "totp": 123456,
  "email_otp": 123456,
  "fido_authentication_response": {},
  "recovery_code": "ABCD-EFGH-IJKL-MNOP"
}'

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import requests

url = "http://api.example.com/auth/login"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
params = {}
payload = {
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "mysecretpassword",
    "totp": 123456,
    "email_otp": 123456,
    "fido_authentication_response": {},
    "recovery_code": "ABCD-EFGH-IJKL-MNOP"
}

response = requests.post(
    url,
    headers=headers,
    params=params,
    json=payload
)

response.raise_for_status()

if response.content:
    print(response.json())

post.description: Make a one-time code for the current user. A desktop app or a script on the same computer uses this code to get its own tokens. The code is linked to the PKCE challenge in the body. The code expires after 60 seconds. A bot cannot make a code. A user who must set up two-factor authentication first cannot make a code.

code_challenge.description: SHA-256 of the PKCE code verifier, encoded in base64url without padding (43 characters)

400.description: The code challenge is not correct

403.description: The token belongs to a bot, or the user must set up two-factor authentication first

post.summary: Change a browser login code into tokens
post.description: Change a one-time browser login code into a new pair of access and refresh tokens. You can use a code one time only. The code verifier must agree with the PKCE challenge of the code. The response has the same shape as the response of a login. This route does not set cookies. The organisation has the chat tokens only for an administrator.

200.description: The user, the organisation and the two tokens

400.description: The code is unknown, expired or used, the verifier is not correct, or the user is inactive

get.summary: Get assets
get.description: Get the assets of the projects that you can access. An administrator gets the assets of all projects. Add a query parameter for each column to filter on. For example, use name=Chair to get the assets with this name. The route /data/assets/all gives the same result. A vendor gets only the assets of their assigned tasks, without the metadata columns hidden from their departments.

403.description: You do not have access to this project

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Get only the assets of this project

parameters.name: entity_type_id
parameters.description: Get only the assets of this asset type

parameters.name: episode_id
parameters.description: Get the assets of this episode and the assets cast in this episode. The project of the episode is used for the access check.

parameters.name: assigned_to
parameters.description: With any value, get only the assets that have a task assigned to you.

get.summary: Get assets with their tasks
get.description: Get the assets of the projects that you can access, with the tasks of each asset. Each asset has its project name and asset type name. Filter with project_id, episode_id or assigned_to. The other columns are not filters on this route. A vendor gets only the assets of their assigned tasks, without the metadata columns hidden from their departments. A client gets the tasks without the studio fields (assignees, estimation, dates, retake count). The response can have an ETag. Send it in If-None-Match to get a 304 response when the data did not change.

400.description: An identifier is not a valid UUID

403.description: You do not have access to this project

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Filter assets by specific project

parameters.name: episode_id
parameters.description: Get the assets of this episode and the assets cast in this episode. Use main to get the assets that have no episode. Use all to get the assets of all episodes.

parameters.name: compact
parameters.description: Encode assets and tasks as positional value arrays (halves the payload). Field names are given by the asset_fields and task_fields entries of the response, map values by name, never by hardcoded position.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream the response as NDJSON (one header line, then one asset per line) instead of a single JSON document, to keep server memory flat on large productions.

parameters.name: assigned_to
parameters.description: With any value, get only the assets that have a task assigned to you.

put.description: Set the casting of one asset in each entity of the list. The entities are shots, assets or episodes of the project. The other assets of each entity do not change. post.summary: Move a comment to another task
post.description: Move a comment to another task of the same entity. The entity can be a shot, an asset, a sequence, an episode or an edit. The comment keeps its text, attachments, mentions, creation date and status change. The notifications and the news of the comment move to the new task. Thus, the watchers of the new task get a notification. You cannot move a comment that is linked to a preview revision. You must have the manager role as your studio role. A manager role given on the project only is not enough. You must have access to the two tasks.

target_task_id.description: Unique identifier of the task to move the comment to. Must belong to the same entity as the current task.

200.description: The moved comment, with its new object_id

400.description: The comment is not on this task, the tasks are on different entities, the two tasks are the same, or the comment is linked to a preview revision

403.description: You are not a studio manager, or you do not have access to one of the tasks

404.description: The task, the target task or the comment does not exist

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the comment's current task

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the comment to move

get.summary: Get person rows
get.description: Get the person rows. All users can call this route. Preview accounts are not in the list. An administrator gets all the fields but the password, the two-factor secrets, the login failure fields and the OIDC and SAML identities. An administrator cannot filter on these fields. With with_pass_hash=true, an administrator also gets the password hash. A client gets only the people of the teams of their open projects, with a short set of fields. The other users get a minimal set of fields. Add a query parameter for each column to filter on, for example first_name=John. An administrator can filter on all the columns but the sensitive ones. The other users can filter only on the fields they get. A user who is not a client can also filter on email. To get the rows that have one value of a list, give the list in JSON.

200.description: The list of person rows, or a page of rows if you give page

400.description: A filter is not valid

parameters.name: with_pass_hash
parameters.description: Include password hash (admin only)

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to get. Without this parameter, the response has all the rows.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of rows in a page. The default value is 100.

parameters.name: relations
parameters.description: Add the related data to each row

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of the fields to get for each row. The response always has id and type. The names that are not fields are ignored.

put.description: Update the fields of a person. Send only the fields to change. You can change your own person. To change another person, you must be an administrator. If you are not an administrator, the route ignores role, departments, active, is_bot, archived, studio_id, last_presence, the login failure fields and the LDAP, OIDC and SAML fields. A bot cannot change its own expiration_date. You cannot change id, created_at, updated_at, password, jti, the two-factor fields and the preview account fields. You cannot change a preview account. You cannot deactivate a protected account of another person or change its role. You cannot activate a person who is not a bot when the user limit is reached. The route checks role, contract_type, country, locale, display_date_format, two_factor_authentication, email and expiration_date. A new expiration date cannot be in the past. When you change expiration_date, the response gives a new access_token, unless the date is in the past. expiration_date uses the YYYY-MM-DD format.

400.description: The body is not valid, a date is not valid, or a field breaks a database constraint

403.description: The person is not you and you are not an administrator, the person is a preview account, or you try to deactivate or change the role of a protected account

404.description: The person does not exist

get.summary: Get the last events
get.description: Get the last events of the event log, the newest first. Use the query parameters to filter the events. To get the next page, give the identifier of the last event in cursor_event_id. An administrator gets the events of all projects. A manager gets the events of their projects only. You must be a manager. A user who has the manager role on a project only must give project_id.

user_id.description: User identifier who triggered the event

400.description: A date or an identifier is not valid

403.description: You are not a manager, you are a manager of this project only and did not give project_id, or you do not have access to this project

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Get the events after this date. Date in the ISO 8601 format, for example 2026-10-28T10:00:00

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Get the events before this date. Date in the ISO 8601 format, for example 2026-10-28T10:00:00

parameters.name: only_files
parameters.description: Get only the events about files

parameters.name: cursor_event_id
parameters.description: Get the events that are older than this event

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events. The maximum value is 1000.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Get only the events of this project

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Get only the events with this name, for example task:update

parameters.name: name_prefixes
parameters.description: Filter events by object, the part of the event name before the colon. Repeat the parameter for each value.

parameters.name: name_suffixes
parameters.description: Filter events by action, the part of the event name after the colon. Repeat the parameter for each value.

parameters.name: person_ids
parameters.description: Filter events by author. Repeat the parameter for each value.

post.description: Create a working file for a task. A working file is a revision of a file that an artist uses to make output files. The route uses the file tree of the project to make the path. If revision is 0, the route uses the next revision. The task is assigned to the current user. A vendor must have a task on the entity of the task. If software_id is not given, the route uses the Blender software and creates it if it does not exist. Only a manager of the project can give person_id to set another author. For other users, the author is always the current user.

400.description: The body is not valid, or the working file already exists

403.description: You do not have access to this project, or you are a vendor without a task on this entity

404.description: The task or the software does not exist

get.summary: Get the time spent of a person for a day, by task
get.description: Get the time spent of a person for a day, with one entry per task. Give project_id to keep the tasks of one project. An administrator and the person get all the tasks. A manager gets the tasks of the projects they manage. A supervisor gets the tasks of the projects they supervise, for the task types of their departments. A supervisor without department gets all the task types. A manager or a supervisor who gives a project_id of another project gets a 403. Other users cannot read the time spents of other persons. You cannot read the time spents of a bot. The manager and supervisor roles are the roles held on the project team.

200.description: The time spent of each task for the day

entity_name.description: Name of the entity of the task

entity_type_name.description: Name of the entity type of the task

duration.description: Time spent on the task in hours

400.description: The date is not valid

403.description: You cannot read the time spents of this person, or the person is a bot, or you cannot access this project

404.description: The person does not exist

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Person unique identifier

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year, for example 2026

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Month, from 1 to 12

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: Day of the month

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Get only the time spent on this project

get.summary: Get the quota shots of a person for a month
get.description: Get the shots that count in the quota of a person for a month. A quota shot is a shot that the person ended. An administrator reads the quotas of all persons. The person reads their own quotas. Give project_id to read the quotas of another person. You must then be a manager or a supervisor in the team of this project. The role held on the project team applies. A manager or a supervisor who gives a project_id of a project they are not a team member of gets a 403, also for their own quotas.

items.description: A serialized shot, with its project_id, full_name and the weight it carries in the period.

400.description: The date or count_mode is not valid

403.description: You cannot read the quotas of this person, or the person is a bot

404.description: The person does not exist

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Person unique identifier

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year, for example 2026

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Month, from 1 to 12

parameters.name: count_mode
parameters.description: How to count the shots: weighted, weighteddone, feedback or done. The default value is weighted. The weighted modes give each shot the part of its work time that is in the period. The other modes count each shot on its end date. The feedback modes end a shot at its first feedback. The done modes end a shot when it is done.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Get only the shots of this project

parameters.name: task_type_id
parameters.description: Get only the shots of this task type

A supervisor gets the tasks of the open projects they supervise, in their departments only. The manager and supervisor roles are the roles held on the project team. If you do not manage or supervise a project, you get an empty list. Without page, the response is a list without order. With page, the response is a page of tasks.

200.description: The list of tasks, or a page of tasks if you give page

is_more.description: True if a later page holds more tasks

400.description: A filter is not valid

403.description: You use a bot token

parameters.name: project_id

parameters.name: task_type_id
parameters.description: Get only the tasks of this task type

parameters.name: task_status_id
parameters.description: Get only the tasks of this task status

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Get only the tasks of these assignees. Give a comma-separated list of person identifiers, or the value unassigned to get the tasks without assignee.

parameters.name: episode_id
parameters.description: Get only the tasks of this episode

parameters.name: due_date_since
parameters.description: Get only the tasks that end on this date or after

parameters.name: due_date_until
parameters.description: Get only the tasks that end on this date or before

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sort order. One of priority, due_date, estimation or entity_name. Another value sorts by project, episode, sequence, entity type, entity and task type names.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to get. A value below 1 is read as 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of tasks in a page. The default value is 100. A value below 1 is read as 1.
